1.title: The Business Case Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module five: The Business Case Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Explain the purpose of the business case practice. Describe its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the project brief, business case, benefits management approach and sustainability management approach. Define output, outcome, benefit, dis-benefit and business objective. Describe the business case lifecycle, aligning products to business objectives and tolerances, and establishing business justification. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The business case practice gives the project a way to judge whether it is (and remains) desirable, viable and achievable, to support decisions about continuing to invest. Desirable. Do the benefits outweigh the costs, risks and dis-benefits? Viable. Can the project be delivered and the benefits realized? Achievable. Can the products be delivered within constraints (time, cost, quality, and so on)? Main principle link: ensure continued business justification. The business case is checked at every decision point.

1.title: Key concepts
1.text: Key concepts. Output. A specialist product the project hands over (for example, a new system). Outcome. The result of change when people use the outputs. Benefit. A measurable improvement perceived as positive by a stakeholder. Dis-benefit. A measurable decline perceived as negative by a stakeholder. Business objective. A target the organization wants to reach that the project supports. Exam tip: Output equals what is delivered. Outcome equals what changes. Benefit equals the measurable gain. Dis-benefit equals the measurable loss. A benefit comes after the project, through use of the outputs.

1.title: Key concepts, continued
1.text: Key concepts. The figure shows this: From outputs to outcomes to benefits.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Project brief. The terms of reference, including the outline business case, used to decide whether to initiate. Business case. The justification for the project: reasons, options, benefits, costs, risks, timescale. Benefits management approach. How benefits will be measured and realized, and by whom (a P I D product). Sustainability management approach. How the project handles environmental, social and economic sustainability targets (a P I D product).

1.title: The lifecycle
1.text: The lifecycle. Develop. An outline business case in the project brief, then a detailed one in the P I D. Verify. The board checks that it is sound and the project is justified. Maintain. Update it with changes, risks and progress; review at each stage end. Confirm. After the project, check whether the benefits were realized. the step names.

1.title: Alignment and justification
1.text: Alignment and justification. Align products to business objectives and tolerances: every product should contribute to a benefit. Establish justification by showing options considered, costs, benefits, risks and timescale. If the case no longer holds, the board should stop the project. Exam tip: Benefits come after the project, when people use the outputs. A question that says benefits are realized on delivery is wrong. Exam tip: The outline business case lives in the project brief; the detailed business case lives in the P I D.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A new payment system is delivered. Which term describes the system itself? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Output. The deliverable is an output.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) A benefit is a measurable improvement seen as positive. (two) A dis-benefit is a measurable decline seen as negative. (three) An outcome is the product the project hands over. (four) A benefit is realized before any outputs are used. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. Statements one and two are correct definitions.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. The business case practice supports decisions about blank the investment. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Continuing. The business case supports decisions about continued investment.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. At which point is an outline business case first created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In the project brief. The outline business case is part of the project brief.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. After the project, the team checks whether promised savings were achieved. Which business case step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Confirm. Checking benefits after the project is confirm.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which management product sets out how benefits will be measured and by whom? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The benefits management approach. That is the purpose of the benefits management approach.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What three questions does the business case answer? Answer: Is the project desirable, viable and achievable? Question two. Define an outcome. Answer: The result of change that comes when people use the outputs. Question three. Define a dis-benefit. Answer: A measurable decline perceived as negative by a stakeholder.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which principle does the business case mainly support? Answer: Ensure continued business justification. Question five. Name the four business case lifecycle steps. Answer: Develop, verify, maintain and confirm. Question six. What does the project brief contain about the business case? Answer: The outline business case.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: judge desirable, viable, achievable; support investment decisions. Terms: output (delivered), outcome (changed), benefit (gain), dis-benefit (loss). Products: project brief, business case, benefits and sustainability management approaches. Lifecycle: develop, verify, maintain, confirm. Principle: ensure continued business justification.
